extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and readers interested in theories of humor (also useful to comedians/writers seeking theoretical insight)
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Veatch's N+V theory to analyze or generate humor by identifying a perceived violation (V), a predominating normal interpretation (N), and their simultaneity (+). Useful for explaining types of laughter (e.g., relief laughter) and for designing joke-generation systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: N+V theory (three conditions necessary and jointly sufficient)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor occurs only when three conditions — N, V, and + — hold: (1) V: something is wrong; (2) N: the situation is actually okay (a predominating normal view); (3) +: both understandings are present simultaneously in the perceiver's mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Veatch claims these three conditions are individually necessary and jointly sufficient for humor; the theory aims to account for diverse phenomena (puns, relief laughter, tickling, group giggles, etc.). The page invites readers to test the claim by finding counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: V — Violation (something is wrong)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an interpretation in which something is wrong: the perceiver thinks things ought to be a certain way — and cares about it — and that expectation is violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: V is an emotionally salient, aversive interpretation (e.g., a perceived moral or physical loss). Examples include the perceived erasure of a caregiver (in infants) or the threat of a mess. The perceiver must care about the violation for it to function as V.

rubrics_metrics.name: N — Normality (situation is actually okay)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a predominating view of the situation as being normal; everything is actually okay — either good or neutral, not bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N provides the reassuring or non-harmful interpretation that coexists with the Violation. The contrast between N and V (not N alone) is what produces the comedic effect. N must be present and sufficiently convincing to negate actual harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: + — Simultaneity (both interpretations present at the same time)
rubrics_metrics.description: The N and V understandings must be present in the perceiver's mind at the same instant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing is crucial: laughter occurs only during the interval when both interpretations coexist; once one interpretation (usually V) is fully reinterpreted or discarded, laughter stops. This temporal overlap is central to the N+V account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional involvement (the perceiver must care)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Violation to serve as V, the perceiver must care about the wrongness — the Violation must generate emotional pain (aversion) in the perceiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theory emphasizes that humor is a form of (cognitively complex) emotional pain that doesn't actually hurt because of the simultaneous N interpretation. Lack of concern about the violation reduces or removes the humorous response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief-laughter mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: A kind of laughter arises when an initially perceived negative event is suddenly reinterpreted as okay (relief) — the perceiver experiences both the initial trauma interpretation and the relief interpretation simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: dropping a sealed milk carton and then realizing no milk spilled leads to a brief, intense laugh that ends when the threat is fully dismissed. Relief laughter exemplifies the N+V dynamics in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peekaboo/object-permanence example (developmental instance of N+V)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a developmental phase (object permanence intermediate stage), a baby treats disappearance as nonexistence (V) yet upon reappearance holds the normal interpretation (N); the simultaneity produces intrinsic humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains the universality of peekaboo: babies in the intermediate object permanence stage have memory but lack current evidence, producing a V that is immediately relieved by N when the caregiver reappears. Later play elaborates timing and teasing to sustain laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for analyzing jokes (identify N and V)
rubrics_metrics.description: To analyze any joke, determine what the emotional Violation (V) is and what the predominating normal interpretation (N) is; if both are present, the theory explains the humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author reports being able to do this for jokes he finds funny (sometimes with effort for jokes he doesn't). Cognitive analysis doesn't prevent initial laughter but can help understand others' humor and why someone laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for machine-generated jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: A machine can generate jokes if it can reason about N and V interpretations and construct situations that encode both interpretations simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no intrinsic reason this cannot be done if AI provides the necessary reasoning infrastructure. The page implies that successful joke-generation systems must create scenarios with a believable Violation and a predominating Normal interpretation that can coexist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation between laughter and crying (valence balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crying may be analogous to laughter but occurs when the Violation interpretation predominates over the Normal interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both responses may involve presence of both interpretations, but which interpretation dominates (V for crying, N for laughter) determines outward emotional response. This provides a criterion for interpreting mixed emotional reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration: structuralist vs absolute N/V distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying N+V, one should consider whether the N/V distinction is a relativistic (graded) structuralist contrast or an absolute, discrete cognitive category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page suggests exploring whether the perception of a Violation is neurologically hardwired or relativistic; this affects how one models N and V and whether a discrete threshold separates them (possible empirical tests via brain imaging).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social/communicative function of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor can serve to relax tense groups, reveal common ground, and function importantly in social animals for communication and group cohesion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theory applies to social uses of humor (e.g., defusing conflict). Studying humor perception profiles might reveal correlations with political, ethnic, age, gender differences; practical use: employing humor to shift group affect.
